_comment: Prose is hand-written; the results blocks are rewritten by tests/sweep_blend.gd. Keep agent ids in step with GameConfig.AGENT_TYPES.

measured.note: One Izzet list mirrored, 19 distinct cards, seats alternated. A model trained on one matchup knows one matchup.

agents.summary: The policy proposes, the search disposes. The network narrows ~30 legal actions to 4, then Greedy's evaluator searches those 4 two plies deep. One network call per decision, at the root only.
capabilities: Learned move ordering plus real minimax — currently the strongest agent here
Cheap where it counts: 4 candidates at depth 2 cost less than 30 at depth 1
Falls back to Greedy if the server dies, and warns once
limits: Assumes the opponent's hand is known — the search cheats at hidden information
Its policy filter is capped by whoever recorded the training games

agents.summary: One-ply search over plans on a hand-written formula: life, board power, card count, mana development. Simulates each plan (land taps + cast) to the end and scores it there, after resolving the stack.
capabilities: The baseline every other agent is measured against, and the fallback for all of them
Resolving the stack before judging (quiescence) is worth ~17 points on its own
No server, no checkpoint, no training data
limits: Judges positions poorly in the abstract, and is inverted before turn 7
Cannot improve — every gain has to be hand-written
One ply: never sees the reply to its own move

agents.summary: Asks the network which of the legal actions a strong player would take, and plays it. One forward pass, no search at all.
capabilities: Trained on the question it is actually asked — which move, given these alternatives
Roughly 300x the supervision of outcome training, from the same recordings
Fast: one small request per decision, state encoded once
limits: 17% against the agent it imitates — pure imitation compounds its own errors
Its ceiling is the strength of whoever recorded the games
Best used as a filter for search, not as a picker

agents.summary: Fixed rule priorities — play a land, cast the biggest thing affordable, attack, block. No search and no simulation.
capabilities: Instant decisions, useful for smoke tests and a varied opponent
Produces more varied positions than either agent against itself
limits: Never simulates the result of a move
Not a valid recording teacher — a model learns 'which agent made this board' from lopsided matchups

agents.summary: Greedy's search with the formula replaced by a network answering 'what is P(the player about to act wins)'. Kept for reference: it judges positions well and picks moves terribly.
capabilities: Ranks positions better than the hand-written formula: 0.800 AUC vs 0.656
Permutation-invariant over card slots, with a learned embedding per card name
Worth retrying as a leaf evaluator inside a deeper search, where it is only ever asked to judge
limits: 6% as a move picker — ranking different positions and ranking the successors of one position are different skills
Outcome training gives one real label per ~300 decisions; every run peaked at epoch 1-2

agents.summary: Picks uniformly from the legal actions. The floor — anything that cannot beat this is broken.
capabilities: Proves the rules engine can finish a game from any sequence of legal actions
